name: N-Ways Addressing for Senegal
status: issued 2026-10-20; open (LICENSING.md); not official, not a postcode, not a land title
firstCriterion: memorability: people already remember a place word and a short number; the address is 'Ouakam 2512', and it is unique in all of Senegal on its own

existingSystems.verdict: postal codes exist but are coarse (delivery-office level, 163 codes) and not door-level; partial physical street addressing in parts of nine cities; the state's door-level Adressage Numérique National (ANN) is in pilot and has published no format

laPoste.format: NNNNN to the left of the delivery office
laPoste.relation: every compound carries laPosteCode (from OSM addr:postcode, or La Poste's list only with La Poste's permission); never embedded in the N-Ways code

streetPlates.format: quartier initials + street number (PE-44, SC-15) and metric door numbers
streetPlates.relation: doors carry streetRef + metricNumber when confirmed

ann.status: relaunched 5-6 Aug 2026, pilot to finish within a year
ann.relation: every compound has annId; the ANN address is shown first once it exists; the registry is offered to the ANN (GOVERNANCE.md)

cadastre.holder: DGID / Direction du Cadastre; PROCASEF (830,000+ parcels in 138 communes by Jun 2026)
cadastre.relation: compound carries nicad and lotissementPlot when known; Add my home imports survey plans

zone.what: 46 frozen code zones: the 45 départements of 2019 (geoBoundaries) with Mbacké split into TBA (arr. Ndame: Touba + Mbacké town) and KTF (Kaël, Taïf)
zone.why: régions are too large (Tambacounda 42,214 km²) and Dakar region too dense for one number space; départements are what people say after the town; frozen so that administrative changes (Keur Massar, 2021) never move a code

lieu.what: the place word: quartier in towns, village in the countryside, cité for estates
lieu.source: OpenStreetMap place nodes (neighbourhood, suburb, village, town, city) and GeoNames populated places; frozen at first issue, curated with the communes as aliases and plate names
lieu.assignment: nearest quartier/village/locality node within 2.5 km in the same zone, else nearest town within 10 km, else nearest place of the zone; decided at first issue and frozen per compound
lieu.duplicates: no context is ever needed: every lieu with the same normalised name, anywhere in Senegal, shares one national number range for that name, one block per lieu (see nationalNameRanges); the zone, the town after a comma and the phone's position are not part of the address. The nearest town of same-named lieux of one zone ('nearTown') is shown on the place card only
lieu.aliases: OSM alt names, parenthesised long names, Wolof and French spellings (Ouakam/Wakam, Mbacké/Mbakke, Thiès/Thies) all resolve
lieu.renamedOrDisputed: the code never changes; a new name is added as an alias

hierarchy.compound: the addressable unit: fenced plot, concession, villa, apartment block, school, market; one number in its lieu's block of the name's national range
hierarchy.structure: a building of the compound: index 1 = largest, then by distance
hierarchy.unit: a flat or a shop door inside a structure

remembered.digits: 3, 4 or 5, never starting with 0; the same length for every lieu of one name
remembered.unique: nationally on its own: 'Médina 12 150' is the Médina of Dakar and 'Médina 23 150' the Médina of Ziguinchor, with no zone or town said
remembered.withdrawn: '<Lieu> <number>, <zone name>' (e.g. 'Medina 150, Ziguinchor') is not used: an address that needs its town to be told apart is not unique
remembered.plateName: the lieu's plate name: at most 12 characters and 2 words (see plateNames)

written.use: plates, stickers, forms; the zone name is information for the reader, not part of the identity; no check letter is ever printed for people
written.officialName: the lieu's full official name is printed in small type under the written form, for context; never required

canonical.check: validate checks the zone key and lieu index against the frozen block table exactly, and the letter over name family + number

spot.use: any point with no compound (field, market pitch, empty plot); computed offline
spot.grid: WGS 84 / UTM 28N, zone frame origin, cell 1/2/5/10 m, 4 or 5 digits per axis

numberLength.rule: per NAME, not per lieu: each lieu of the name needs a block of 3 x compounds rounded up to the grain (10 for 3 digits, 100 for 4-5 digits, at least one grain); digits = smallest d in {3,4,5} for which the blocks fill at most 90 % of the d-digit range
numberLength.spare: at least 10 % of every name's range stays unallocated at first issue, for new lieux of the same name: 90 / 900 / 9,000 numbers
numberLength.overflow: a full block takes a further block from the name's spare space, then '<Lieu> Extension' (official name), a new name with its own national range; its plate name is chosen by the commune when '<plate> Extension' is over the limit
numberLength.split: a lieu over 27,000 compounds is split along named sub-quartiers before first issue

plateNames.rule: a long address is not remembered, so the name in the remembered code is a PLATE name of at most 12 characters (NFC; letters, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes count one; an accented letter is one) and at most 2 words (linking words de/du/des/d'/la/le/les/l'/et/sur/en/au/aux/à/& do not count; a hyphen separates words); a trailing sector numeral counts in the characters, not as a word ('Liberté 6', 'HLM 5')

names.officialName: the full name from the map or the commune list: small print on cards and plates, accepted when typed (alias)
names.name: the plate name used in the code

derivation: documented short form with a source (known)

clean: numeral split off and written in digits; generic words (quartier, village de, hameau, lotissement, zone, secteur, campement) and scheme labels (S.I.C.A.P., Sicap) dropped; brackets, text after a slash, a second spelling after ou dropped; acronym dots removed
else: runs of whole words that fit, ranked by rarity over all lieu names; the best taken only when clearly ahead (distinctive)
else, or when a Senegal rule applies: needsCouncilChoice with up to 3 candidates, the first used provisionally

senegalRules.cite: 'Cité' is kept in a name that fits ('Cité Lamy'); it only goes first when the name is too long
toCommune: settlement heads of a person's, family's or holy place's name: Keur/Kër/Kerr, Darou/Dar, Médina/Madina, Médinatoul, Djannatoul, Boukhatoul, Saré, Sinthiou (and spellings), Sinthiang, Santhie, Gourel, Ouro/Wouro, Dara, Touba, Taïba, Missira, Hamdallaye, Baïti/Beyti
given names, family names and initials (Mamadou, Ousmane, Ndiaye, Diop, Fall, M.)
ethnic, compass and land qualifiers (Peul, Wolof, Sérère, Toucouleur, Bambara, Diola, Nord, Sud, Est, Ouest, Centre, Walo, Diéri, Ferlo, Kounda) and descriptive nouns (Marché, Gare, Plage...)
joined names of several quartiers and 'X de Y' names
a result equal to a commune or département seat, a regional capital or a large city of the region (not the lieu's own town; regional capitals and large cities are never own)
a result equal to another lieu of the same zone
short forms said but not documented ('Parcelles' for Parcelles Assainies)

plateNames.aliases: the official name and other spellings are aliases; an alias claimed by two plate names is dropped (aliasesDropped in lieux.json)
plateNames.ranges: same-normalised plate names share one national range (nationalNameRanges)
plateNames.council: a flagged lieu keeps a provisional plate name (its first candidate) so that it can be numbered; the commune confirms or replaces it, and the number does not change
plateNames.engine: plate_ok / split_numeral in sn_engine.py; allocate_families and Lieux.add_lieu refuse a plate over the limit unless flagged

nationalNameRanges.rule: a remembered address is said without its town, so it must be unique nationally on its own, with no context: two quartiers called Médina cannot both have a Médina 150
nationalNameRanges.model: every lieu whose plate name folds to the same name key belongs to one name family; the family has ONE national number range, cut into one block per lieu; 'name + number' falls in exactly one block, so it decodes to one lieu and one compound anywhere in Senegal

normalisation.language: French and Wolof (official Wolof orthography, décret 2005-992), applied to every place word
steps: ñ -> ny, œ -> oe, æ -> ae; accents and case removed
hyphens, apostrophes, dots, brackets -> spaces; St/Ste/Sainte -> saint
trailing numeral dropped (with numero/no): HLM, HLM 2 ... HLM 6 are one name; Pikine and Pikine 3 are one name
leading articles and generic words dropped when something follows: le, la, les, l', de, du, d', quartier, village, hameau (Cité is kept)

French/Wolof spelling folded: ou+vowel -> w (Ouakam = Wakam); ou -> u (Darou = Daru); eu -> e (Keur = Kër); kh -> x; th -> t; ph -> f; dj, di+vowel -> j (Ndiaye = Njaay); gn -> ny; c+e/i/y -> s; ck/qu/q/c -> k (Mbacké = Mbakke); y -> i; silent h dropped (Hamdallaye = Amdalaye)
doubled letters collapsed (Gounass = Gounas), final silent e dropped (Ndiayène = Ndiayene)
normalisation.why: deliberately generous: names people can confuse by ear or spelling must share one range, or two places would have the same remembered address; over-folding only lengthens a range

nationalNameRanges.blocks: cut from the bottom of the name's range, one per lieu, in (zone key, lieu index) order; e.g. Médina (9 lieux, 5 digits): Dakar 10400-17799, Saint-Louis 19600-22899, Ziguinchor 22900-23399, free 23400-99999
nationalNameRanges.numeral: the trailing numeral of a name stays in the place word ('HLM 5 17 395'); decoding takes the last d digits of the name's length as the number, and any digits before must be the lieu's own numeral ('HLM 17395' = 'HLM 5 17 395'; 'HLM 3 17395' refused)

qualifiers.rule: names whose lieux together do not fit 5 digits: the largest take ONE established qualifier people already say (as 'Médina Baye' is a name of its own), decided once per name with the commune and listed; never a zone name at the end, never an ordinal
qualifiers.today: none needed with the 2026-10-18 counts; the fullest 5-digit range is Darou Salam, 75.1 % allocated

nationalNameRanges.stability: the block table is frozen at first issue: blocks are never renumbered, moved or shrunk; a new lieu with an existing name gets a new block from the name's spare space; a full block gets a further block of one grain; a renamed lieu keeps its block
nationalNameRanges.checkLetter: computed over the name family id + number; the lieu is bound by the block table (one lieu per number of a name), so a one-digit slip into another same-named lieu's block changes one payload position and is always caught

checkLetter.method: ISO/IEC 7064 MOD 11-2 over name family id (5 digits) + number (5, zero-padded); spot codes: zone index + E + N digits
checkLetter.lettersReason: French letter names: one of each rhyming set (no B C D G P V; T kept), one of each e-e pair (F, M, R), J kept and G dropped (gé/ji), no vowels, no Y, no O/I/L
checkLetter.detects: every single wrong digit and every swap of adjacent digits, including a slip into another same-named lieu's block

spoken.fr: place word, then the number as a house number (3 digits: 'cent vingt') or in pairs like phone numbers (4: 'quarante-cinq, douze'; 5: 'quarante-cinq, cent vingt-huit')
spoken.wo: place word, then digits one by one (benn, ñaar, ñett, ñeent, juróom…); Wolof 3/4 and 8/9 sound alike, so the app reads the code back
spoken.otherLanguages: Pulaar, Serer, Jola, Mandinka speakers use the same place word and French or Wolof digits

rules.name: enclosure
rules.condition: centroid inside an OSM wall/fence, an N-Ways gated site, an Add-my-home outline or a cadastral parcel
rules.estates: a cité with one gate becomes the estate of the compounds inside, not one compound

rules.name: satellite
rules.condition: footprint < 30 m² within 4 m (urban) / 8 m (rural) of a structure >= 30 m²

rules.name: rural concession
rules.condition: rural fabric, footprints < 120 m², gap <= 6 m, at most 30 structures

rules.name: people
rules.condition: the building's owner + 1, or 2 independent confirmations: 'one home' / 'separate home'

compounds.urbanFabric: >= 100 structures in the 250 m UTM tile (1,600/km²)
compounds.neverMerged: two main structures (>= 30 m²) in urban fabric by shape alone: wall-to-wall houses in the Médina, Pikine or Touba are separate concessions
compounds.gap: centroid distance minus equivalent-circle radii sqrt(area/pi)
compounds.gate: primary entrance; navigation ends there; sources: confirmed door > Add my home > OSM gate/entrance > N-Ways routing gates

fields.heightM: OSM height, else OSM building:levels x 3.0 m, else null (the ML h is a rendering filler and is never used)
fields.floors: OSM building:levels, else height / 3.0 m, else 1 (source 'default')
fields.floorAreaM2: footprint x floors (estimate flag when floors is default)
fields.name: businesses and public buildings only
fields.sources: per attribute: osm:<tag>, ml:footprint, places:<category>, people, partner:<name>, default

classes.res.annexe: annexe (kitchen, toilets, store, gatehouse, boys' quarters)
classes.gov.admin: administration (ministère, gouvernance, préfecture, mairie, police, gendarmerie, poste)
classes.edu.daara: daara (only from tags, places or people)

buildingProfile.inference: SPEC.md section 6.2: OSM tags (0.85-0.9) > N-Ways places inside the footprint (0.6-0.7) > shape and height (0.2-0.5); people's confirmations set 0.95

private: household counts (kept only as one/several, shown to nobody)
Add-my-home photos (kept for verification, not published)
doors a household asked to hide
privacy.law: Loi 2008-12 and Décret 2008-721; authority: CDP; geolocation processing declared before launch (déclaration normale)

steps: gate: GPS averaged 10 s + one gate photo

outline: (a) tap corners on imagery, (b) walk inside the wall with ARKit/ARCore, (c) import survey-plan beacons (Yoff/UTM 28N EPSG:31028, NSGD2004/UTM 28N or WGS 84/UTM 28N EPSG:32628) + NICAD or lotissement plot
provisional address: next reserved number in the lieu's block (midpoint between Hilbert neighbours), else a further block from the name's spare space, else '<Lieu> Extension'
confirmed: a delivery/arrival by someone else, 30 days without a neighbour's dispute, or new imagery/footprints
safeguards: an address, not a land title (stated in the flow)
gate on the outline, area 20-20,000 m², closed loop, GPS vs AR within 5 m, imported plan within 30 m of the gate
keeps outline + gate position + gate photo only; no video, no interior
offline: spot code at once; the address is issued by the registry on the next connection
addMyHome.legal: Law 64-46 (domaine national), Law 2011-07 (titre foncier); only the cadastre and géomètres-experts survey for titles; N-Ways never decides land disputes
addMyHome.officialAreas: status 'provisional-alias': no N-Ways plate; the household is told to ask the commune for the official number

channels: N-Ways app: 'Votre adresse' shown as soon as home is known; one tap to share by WhatsApp or SMS link
partners (couriers, banks, utilities) look up a customer's address with the customer's consent
getting.laterOption: an SMS lookup service (possible later option, not planned now)

dataProtection.law: Loi n° 2008-12 du 25 janvier 2008; Décret n° 2008-721
dataProtection.authority: Commission de protection des données personnelles (CDP)
dataProtection.reform: replacement bill (APDP) pending since 2019; no adoption found as of 2026-10-18 (unverified absence)

governance: N-WAYS LIMITED maintains it and is the single issuer; hand-over to the ANN or a body it designates; see GOVERNANCE.md

coverageMask.rule: where a government address system exists (even partial), use the government's data and show its address as written: an official address is the one people are legally held to; N-Ways addresses only where nothing official exists

levels.ann: ANN address shown as written; N-Ways address is an alias
levels.official-municipal: municipal street addressing (street codes such as PE-44, metric door numbers) shown as written; N-Ways address shown only as temporary until the official number is obtained; no N-Ways plates
levels.nways: N-Ways address proposed, plates and stickers

evidence: official dataset from a commune, ARTP, ADM or the ANN
>= 3 OSM streets in the lieu with programme street references (1,601 such streets nationally)
official plates confirmed by people at sampled doors
coverageMask.growth: the mask only grows; when official coverage reaches an N-Ways lieu, its addresses are retired as primary and kept as aliases resolving to the official address (crosswalk); never reissued
coverageMask.notInMask: La Poste 5-digit postcodes (delivery-office level): the door-level model applies, every compound maps to its laPosteCode
